lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 18 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 18 and in approved education
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let's begin. To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you some questions about your child.

**First, how old is your child?**

This will help me understand which eligibility criteria apply:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Those aged 20 or over typically don't qualify

Please tell me your child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have a son, Alex, who's 18 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! You have a son named Alex who is 18 years old.

Since Alex is 18 (which falls in the 16-19 age range), he may still qualify for Child Benefit if he meets certain education or training requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to ask about Alex's education or training status:**

Is Alex currently:
1. **In approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education, or approved vocational training), OR
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks), OR
3. **Neither** of the above (not in education/training and didn't recently leave)?

Please let me know which situation applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, which is approved education. Let me check the education level requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! A-levels at sixth form college is considered **approved non-advanced education**, which is good news for Child Benefit eligibility.

Now I need to check a few more things:

**1. Is Alex studying full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

**2. Is Alex's course funded or arranged by an employer,** or does he have an agreed future job with an employer who's funding the course?

**3. Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?** (If yes, I'd need to know if he's financially dependent on you)

Please let me know the answers to these questions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying full-time at the college - it's a proper full-time A-level course. No, it's not anything to do with an employer, just regular sixth form. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's all great news. Alex's A-level course meets all the education requirements:
- ✓ Full-time education (12+ hours per week)
- ✓ Approved non-advanced qualification (A-levels)
- ✓ Not employer-funded
- ✓ Not married

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week** (or not in paid work at all)?

For Child Benefit purposes, young people aged 16-19 in education cannot be working 24 or more hours per week.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's just focused on his studies.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is focused on his studies and not working, which is perfectly fine for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** Specifically, benefits like:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Income Support
- Tax credits

If Alex is NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right, that's fine for Child Benefit purposes.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not getting any benefits himself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own right.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! One more question about Alex's education:

**Is Alex doing an apprenticeship?**

Most apprenticeships disqualify from Child Benefit (such as apprenticeships in England and Modern Apprenticeships in Scotland), though there are some exceptions like Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales.

Since you mentioned he's doing A-levels at sixth form college, I'm assuming this is NOT an apprenticeship - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, it's not an apprenticeship - just regular A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is doing regular A-levels, not an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check about **your** eligibility as the claimant. 

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If you do, that satisfies the residency requirement. If not, there are some special circumstances that might apply (such as having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or being a Crown servant abroad).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK, which meets the residency requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means either:
1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards his care - this could include food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc.), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** for Alex under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex lives at home with you, which clearly establishes your responsibility for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

If someone else is claiming, it's important to know whether they would agree to transfer the claim to you, or if there would be a dispute about who should claim.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In hospital** (admitted as an inpatient)?
2. **In local authority care** (placed in care by the council)?
3. **Fostered** (living with foster parents)?
4. **Living normally** at home with you?

Which of these describes Alex's situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

If the council is NOT paying for Alex (which is typically the case for children living at home with their parents), then you should be eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**You meet all the eligibility requirements for claiming Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** because:
- He's 18 years old (within the 16-19 age range)
- He's studying full-time for A-levels at sixth form college (approved non-advanced education)
- He's not working (or working less than 24 hours per week)
- He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- He's not doing an apprenticeship

✅ **You qualify as a claimant** because:
- You normally live in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex (he lives with you)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- The local council isn't paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate

### Important Information:

⚠️ **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay some or all of the Child Benefit back through tax. However, you can still claim it to protect your National Insurance credits, or you can choose not to receive payments.

💷 **Payment Schedule**: Child Benefit is typically paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits).

📋 **For more information and to apply**: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about claiming or the process?
